subject: Pay-to-Park Program Updates
overview: The Council discussed operational adjustments to the new pay-to-park system and initiated a rezoning study for the Meadow Glen Mall site. They also requested urgent updates on the future of Lawrence Memorial Hospital following a court ruling against its proposed merger.

items.title: Parking contract resolution
items.summary: A resolution regarding the Mayor's authority to negotiate a parking contract was tabled and subsequently withdrawn by the sponsor.

items.title: Law Department claim settlement
items.summary: Approved a $5,000 settlement for Nancy J. Avalone regarding a sidewalk defect injury on Governor's Avenue. The Council requested a DPW update on repair status and ground stability in the area.

items.title: Tiered water and sewer rate structure
items.summary: Approved a resolution acknowledging a revised tiered billing system intended to provide more equity for residential ratepayers by increasing tier thresholds. Discussion addressed how these rates intersect with conservation goals and a reported $8.5 million department surplus.

items.title: Classic Cafe license and rink safety
items.summary: Approved a common victualler's license for Classic Cafe at 174 Spring Street and safety improvements, including a flashing light and crosswalk painting, at Le Conte Rink.

items.title: Meadow Glen Mall and Shaw's site rezoning
items.summary: Approved a request for the Office of Community Development to examine mixed-use development rezoning options for the Meadow Glen Mall and former Shaw's Supermarket sites. The proposal aims to revitalize the Route 16 corridor through integrated commercial and residential uses.

items.title: Commendations and police department update
items.summary: Approved commendations for baseball coaches John McGonigal and Lonnie Hilson Sr., and congratulated Lieutenant Michael Goulding on his selection as the new Police Chief for the Town of Weston.

items.title: Hallmark Health and Partners merger update
items.summary: Approved a request for representatives from Hallmark Health and the Attorney General's office to update the Council on next steps following a court ruling blocking the Partners Health merger. Members expressed concern regarding the future solvency and service levels at Lawrence Memorial Hospital.

items.title: Salem Street property and business district roundtable
items.summary: Approved a request for the Building Department to report on a fire-damaged property on Salem Street and called for a roundtable discussion on revitalizing the city's five main business districts.

items.title: Malden Hospital property and Held Circle cell tower
items.summary: Discussed the potential development of the former Malden Hospital property and approved a request for information from the Building Department regarding the ownership and safety of a cell tower on Held Circle.

items.title: Pay-to-park program operational updates
items.summary: Chief Sacco announced that parking enforcement hours will change from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. following a legal opinion from the City Solicitor. The Council requested data on meals tax revenue and a legal opinion on whether the Traffic Commission can implement a 15-minute free parking window citywide.

items.title: Ceremonial resolutions and announcements
items.summary: The Council congratulated Father Kevin Toomey on his service, celebrated recent births in the Marino and Mayako families, and approved the minutes of the January 20 meeting.
